content.text:
I submitted index 0 (Fe 0.84, Sb 0.16) as the best composition. At 0.077% it had the highest EQE of the three I measured, but that is still very low in absolute terms.

| Index | Composition | EQE |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Fe 0.84 / Sb 0.16 | **0.077%** |
| 2 | Fe 0.80 / Sb 0.20 | 0.052% |
| 14 | Fe 0.48 / Sb 0.52 | 0.015% |

- **Trend:** EQE went up as the Fe content went up. Index 0 is the most Fe-rich composition in the library, so the trend can't be followed any further.
- **Model checks:**
  - MACE puts hematite (Fe₂O₃) on the hull, and MEGNet predicts a 2.77 eV band gap. Hematite can therefore absorb the 3.2 eV light.
  - FeSbO₄ is also predicted stable (0.0016 eV/atom above the hull) with a 2.08 eV gap, but the film near that composition (index 14) performed worst of the three.
- **Not measured:** I didn't measure any of the Sb-rich compositions (indices 20–29), because EQE fell as Sb increased. The model suggested index 7, near the middle of the range, where it was least certain. It predicted a low value there, so I measured index 0 instead.
- **Unused:** I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements, so the phases in these films were never confirmed.

With only three measurements, I can't rule out a better composition in an unmeasured region, especially the middle of the range.
